texts.preamble: Balmukund Garg vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 23 November, 2019 Equivalent citations: Aironline 2019 Mp 1870 Author: Vandana Kasrekar Bench: Vandana Kasrekar
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. seeking quashment of the F.I.R. bearing Crime No.255/19 dated 24.08.2019(Annexure-P/1) registered at Police Station Sendhwa City, District - Barwani for offence under Sections 420, 272, 273 of IPC and under Sections 3 & 7 of Essential Commodities Act(in short .... "the Act"). 2. That, the petitioner's father is running a firm in the name of Balmukund Mohanlal having registration with Food Department. That the proprietor of the said firm is in the business of Retail Sale purchase of the permitted items. 3. On 5/08/2019 the officers of the food department made a raid on the premises of the firm Balmukund Mohanlal and seized certain material and, thereafter, the respondent no.1 in the utter violation of the provisions of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 has registered the criminal case against the petitioner without application of mind and has filed the charge-sheet.
texts.arguments: It is alleged that since the petitioner is not the authorized person of the firm Balmukund Mohanlal, therefore, cannot be held responsible for any act. Even otherwise the respondent no.2 without following the provision of the Act of HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH :INDORE BENCH (Balmukund Garg Vs. State of M.P. & Anr.) 2006 and the Rules made there-under has directly referred the matter to the police authority, whereas the Act itself provides for filing of the prosecution after taking due sanction. Being aggrieved by the action of the respondents in registering the F.I.R., the petitioner has preferred this petition for quashing the F.I.R. registered against him. Balmukund Garg vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 23 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20264940/ 1 4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that there is no evidence available on record against the present petitioners to frame charges under Sections 420, 272, 273 of IPC and under Sections 3 & 7 of the Essential Commodities Act. He submits that the petitioner is not the authorized person of the firm on whose premises the raid was made. He further submits that the F.I.R. has been registered by the police authority on the basis of a false and cooked up story of the complainant and unnecessarily impleaded the petitioner as accused, without investigating the matter. He further submits that the provisions of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006(in short ...."the Act of 2006") makes it amply clear that prescribed procedure has to be followed for prosecuting the offence after taking the sanction, but the respondent no.2 without adhering or in the utter violation of the provisions of the Act and the Rules specially constituted for the nature of the offences as alleged in the present case has filed the report to the police for taking action. No procedure was followed ever as required under the Act. He submits that even if the allegations mentioned in the FIR is taken at their face value and accepted in the entirety, then also it does not prima-facie constitute any offence against the petitioner. He HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH :INDORE BENCH (Balmukund Garg Vs. State of M.P. & Anr.) also submits that the allegation in the F.I.R. and other material does not disclose any cognizable offence against the petitioner. Therefore, he submits that the FIR/charges framed against the petitioner is required to be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 5. Learned counsel for the respondents supports the order passed by the Court below and submits that the charges have been rightly framed against the petitioner. The Act of 2006 makes it amply clear that prescribed procedure has to be followed for prosecuting an HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH :INDORE BENCH (Balmukund Garg Vs. State of M.P. & Anr.) offender, before taking any cognizance under the Act, but the same has not been followed by the respondent in the present case.
